Healthy Start Program Eligibility and Enrollment Policy
Document type/version: policy document

Where the number of applications exceeds available program slots, priority will be given to applicants who fall within one or more of the following categories. Priority categories are listed in descending order of precedence:

a) Applicants under the age of 18 years (adolescent pregnancies).

b) Applicants over the age of 35 years (advanced maternal age).

c) Applicants with a history of complicated pregnancy, including but not limited to: previous caesarean section, pre-eclampsia, eclampsia, gestational diabetes, or postpartum hemorrhage.

d) Applicants with a known chronic illness, such as hypertension, diabetes, HIV, or sickle cell disease.

e) Applicants from households with a monthly income below the national minimum wage, or households that are food-insecure as determined by the HBCHI household screening tool.

f) Applicants with no prior antenatal care in any facility during the current pregnancy.

3.3 Ineligibility

An applicant shall be deemed ineligible if any of the following conditions apply:

a) The applicant is not a resident of the operational catchment area as defined in Section 3.1(b).

b) The applicant is not pregnant and does not have an infant under six (6) months of age.

c) The applicant has previously been disenrolled from the Healthy Start Program for cause, including but not limited to fraud, misrepresentation of information, or repeated non-compliance with program requirements. Disenrollment for cause shall be permanent unless the applicant successfully appeals the decision through the process outlined in Section 7.

d) The applicant has been found to have provided false or misleading information on the application form or during the verification process. Such applicants shall be barred from re-applying for a period of twelve (12) months from the date of discovery.

4. REQUIRED DOCUMENTATION FOR ENROLLMENT

Applicants must submit the following documentation at the time of application. Failure to submit complete documentation will delay processing of the application.

4.1 Proof of Residency

A valid means of identification showing the applicant's residential address, or a letter of confirmation from the CHEW responsible for the applicant's ward. The letter must be on letterhead and include the CHEW's signature, official stamp, and contact telephone number.

4.2 Income Verification

For applicants applying under priority category 3.2(e), proof of household income must be provided. Acceptable forms include:

a) Payslip from current employer (if formally employed), dated within the last three (3) months.

b) A self-declaration of income on the HBCHI income declaration form, countersigned by the ward head or a recognized community leader.

c) For self-employed or informally employed applicants, a letter of attestation from a community leader or the CHEW confirming the applicant's economic status.

4.3 Antenatal Visit Records

a) A copy of the applicant's antenatal care (ANC) card or clinic record, if any ANC visits have been conducted. If the applicant has not yet attended any ANC visit, this requirement is waived, and the applicant shall be referred for a first ANC visit upon enrollment.

b) For applicants transferring from another facility, a referral letter or a summary of ANC records from the previous facility. Where the previous facility is not able to provide records, the applicant may provide a verbal history, which shall be documented by the enrolling officer.
5.3 Certified Clinic Definition

For the purposes of this policy, a certified clinic is a health facility that meets the following criteria:

a) It is registered with the State Ministry of Health or the relevant local government health authority.

b) It has at least one qualified midwife, nurse, or community health officer on staff who is trained in antenatal care.

c) It has the basic equipment and supplies needed to conduct antenatal examinations, including a blood pressure machine, a fetoscope or Doppler, and weighing scales.

d) It has been certified by the HBCHI program office as a participating clinic for the Healthy Start Program. A list of certified clinics is maintained by the program office and is available to all enrolling officers. The list is updated quarterly.

A clinic that is registered with the State Ministry of Health but has not been certified by the HBCHI program office is not considered a certified clinic for the purposes of this policy. However, an applicant who has attended an antenatal visit at such a clinic may still be eligible if the clinic is subsequently certified before the date of the applicant's enrollment. In such cases, the enrolling officer shall note the certification date in the applicant's file.

5.4 Verification of Clinic Certification

Healthy Start Program eligibility_requires_antenatal_visit is at least one antenatal visit at a certified clinic. Record status: current.

Enrolling officers shall verify the certification status of a clinic using the following methods:

a) Consult the current list of certified clinics, which is available in the program office and on the HBCHI intranet. The list is updated quarterly, and the date of the last update shall be noted on the list.

b) If the clinic is not on the list, the enrolling officer shall contact the program office by phone or email to confirm whether the clinic has been certified. The program office shall respond within two working days.

c) If the clinic is not certified, the applicant shall be informed that the antenatal visit does not meet the requirement. The applicant shall be given the opportunity to attend an antenatal visit at a certified clinic before the application deadline, if time permits.

d) In cases where the applicant has attended an antenatal visit at a clinic that is not certified, but the applicant is otherwise eligible, the enrolling officer may recommend that the applicant be allowed to enroll on a provisional basis, subject to the applicant attending a first antenatal visit at a certified clinic within four weeks of enrollment. Provisional enrollment is at the discretion of the program director and shall be documented in the applicant's file.

5.5 Timing of the Antenatal Visit

The antenatal visit must have occurred within the current pregnancy. For applicants who are not yet pregnant but are applying for the program as part of family planning or preconception care, the antenatal visit requirement is waived. In such cases, the applicant shall be referred for a first antenatal visit upon becoming pregnant.

For applicants who are pregnant but have not yet attended any antenatal visit, the requirement is not waived. The applicant must attend at least one antenatal visit at a certified clinic before the application can be approved. The enrolling officer shall refer the applicant to a certified clinic and shall note the referral in the applicant's file. The applicant shall provide proof of the visit within two weeks of the referral, or before the application deadline, whichever is earlier.
If the applicant is unable to provide any of the above documents, the enrolling officer shall record the reason in the applicant's file and shall refer the matter to the program office for a determination. The program office may accept alternative proof of income on a case-by-case basis.

5.6.2 Calculation of Income for Self-Employed Applicants

For self-employed applicants, monthly income shall be calculated as the average of the applicant's net income over the three months preceding the application date. Net income shall be the gross receipts of the business less the direct costs of goods sold and operating expenses. The applicant shall provide a breakdown of these figures in the sworn affidavit of income. The enrolling officer may request additional documentation if the figures provided are not consistent with the bank statements or other records submitted.

In cases where the applicant's income fluctuates significantly from month to month, the enrolling officer shall note this in the applicant's file and shall calculate the average monthly income over the three-month period. If the applicant has been self-employed for less than three months, the calculation shall be based on the period for which records are available, and the enrolling officer shall note this in the applicant's file.

5.6.3 Household Income

For the purpose of this policy, household income shall include the income of the applicant and the applicant's spouse, if any, and any other adult who regularly contributes to the household's expenses. The applicant shall declare all sources of household income on the application form. The enrolling officer may request proof of income from any person whose income is included in the household income calculation.

Where the applicant is married but the spouse does not contribute to the household income, the applicant shall provide a written explanation, and the enrolling officer may accept this explanation if it is reasonable in the circumstances.

5.6.4 Changes in Income

The enrolling officer shall recalculate eligibility based on the new income figure. If the applicant's income increases above the threshold after enrollment, the applicant shall remain enrolled for the remainder of the enrollment period, but may not be eligible for renewal.

5.7 Documentation of Eligibility

The enrolling officer shall record in the applicant's file the basis for the determination of eligibility, including the documents reviewed and the income figure used. The file shall also contain a copy of the application form and all supporting documents. The enrolling officer shall date and sign the eligibility determination.

5.8 Approval of Applications

The enrolling officer shall approve an application if the applicant meets all the eligibility criteria set out in this policy. The approval shall be recorded on the application form and in the applicant's file. The enrolling officer shall issue an enrollment card to the applicant within five working days of the approval.
Residency is verified through official documents. All documents submitted shall be current and shall bear the applicant's name and a residential address within one of the eligible districts.

Primary documents:

a. A valid National Identity Card or National Identity Number slip showing the applicant's residential address;
b. A current utility bill (electricity, water, or waste disposal) issued within the last three months, showing the applicant's name and address;

Secondary documents (may be used as the second document):

a. A bank statement issued within the last three months showing the applicant's address;
b. A voter's card issued by the Independent National Electoral Commission;
c. A tax clearance certificate or tax payment receipt issued within the last twelve months;
d. A letter from the applicant's employer confirming the applicant's residential address and period of employment;
e. A motor vehicle licence or motorcycle registration document showing the applicant's address;

The enrolling officer shall examine each document for consistency. Where documents show different addresses, the enrolling officer shall ask the applicant to explain the discrepancy. If the explanation is satisfactory and at least one primary document shows an address within an eligible district, the application may proceed. If no document shows an address within an eligible district, the application shall be rejected on the ground of failure to meet the residency requirement.

5.9.4 Alternative Verification Procedure

An applicant who is unable to provide any of the primary documents listed above may request an alternative verification. The applicant shall explain in writing why the documents are not available. Acceptable reasons include: the applicant has never been issued a National Identity Card; the applicant lives in a family compound where utility bills are in the name of a relative; the applicant is a recent widow or widower and the documents are in the name of the deceased spouse; or the applicant's home is in an area where utility services are not individually metered.

In such cases, the enrolling officer shall conduct a home visit within seven working days of the request. The home visit shall be conducted by the enrolling officer and, where practicable, a second member of staff. During the visit, the enrolling officer shall:

a. Confirm that the applicant occupies the dwelling and that the dwelling is within an eligible district;
b. Interview the applicant and, where available, a neighbour or the head of the compound to confirm the period of residence;
c. Record the findings on a standard Home Visit Report form, which shall include the date of the visit, the names and signatures of the staff conducting the visit, and a description of the dwelling and its location;
d. Obtain the applicant's signature on the completed form.
d. A recent change in the applicant's circumstances that could not reasonably have been foreseen at the time of application, such as the death of a spouse, loss of employment, or a change in the applicant's place of residence which was beyond the applicant's control;

e. Any other ground which the Program Director determines, in her sole discretion, to constitute exceptional circumstances.

The existence of one or more of these grounds does not oblige the Program Director to grant an exception. The Program Director shall consider each request on its merits, taking into account the purpose of the Program, the availability of resources, and the fairness of granting the exception relative to other applicants.

2. The completed form shall be submitted to the enrolling officer at the centre where the applicant originally applied, or, if the applicant has not yet applied, to the centre in the applicant's district of residence. The form shall be accompanied by:

a. A written statement setting out the grounds for the request and the specific criterion or criteria for which the exception is sought;

c. The applicant's contact details, including a telephone number and, where available, an address for the delivery of correspondence.

3. The enrolling officer shall acknowledge receipt of the request in writing within two working days. The acknowledgement shall include the date of receipt and a reference number for the request.

4. The enrolling officer shall review the request to confirm that it is complete. If any document is missing, the enrolling officer shall notify the applicant in writing and allow ten working days for the applicant to supply the missing document. Where the exception is granted, the notification shall state the specific criterion or criteria to which the exception applies and any conditions attached to the exception. Where the exception is refused, the notification shall state the reasons for the refusal.
9. ENROLLMENT PROCEDURE

The enrollment procedure is set out below. The steps are to be followed in the order given, and no step may be omitted or reordered without the prior written approval of the Program Director.

Step 1 – Expression of Interest. An applicant who wishes to enrol in the Healthy Start Program shall submit a written Expression of Interest to the enrolling officer at the health facility nearest to the applicant's place of residence. The Expression of Interest may be submitted in person or by post. It shall include the applicant's full name, date of birth, address, and the name of the head of household, if the applicant is a minor or is applying as part of a household.

Step 2 – Preliminary Screening. Upon receipt of the Expression of Interest, the enrolling officer shall conduct a preliminary screening to determine whether the applicant appears to meet the eligibility criteria set out in Sections 3, 4, and 5 of this Policy. The preliminary screening shall be based solely on the information contained in the Expression of Interest and any supporting documents submitted with it. The enrolling officer shall not require the applicant to provide additional information at this stage unless the Expression of Interest is incomplete on its face.

Step 3 – Invitation to Apply. Where the preliminary screening indicates that the applicant may be eligible, the enrolling officer shall issue a formal Application Form (Form HSP-AP-01) to the applicant. The Application Form shall be issued within five working days of the preliminary screening. Where the preliminary screening indicates that the applicant is not eligible, the enrolling officer shall notify the applicant in writing of the reasons for the refusal, and shall inform the applicant of the right to request an exception under Section 8 of this Policy.

Step 4 – Submission of Application. The applicant shall complete the Application Form and return it to the enrolling officer, together with the supporting documents listed in Section 7 of this Policy. The application shall be submitted within twenty working days of the date of issue of the Application Form. If the application is not submitted within this period, the invitation to apply shall lapse, and the applicant shall be required to begin the process again with a new Expression of Interest.

Step 5 – Verification. On receipt of the completed Application Form, the enrolling officer shall verify the information contained in it. The verification shall include, where practicable, a home visit to confirm the applicant's place of residence and household composition. The enrolling officer shall also verify the authenticity of the supporting documents, and may contact the issuing authorities for this purpose. The verification shall be completed within fifteen working days of receipt of the application.

Step 6 – Eligibility Determination. Upon completion of the verification, the enrolling officer shall determine whether the applicant meets the eligibility criteria. The determination shall be recorded on Form HSP-EL-01, which shall be signed and dated by the enrolling officer. Where the determination is that the applicant is eligible, the enrolling officer shall forward the file to the Program Director's office for final approval. Where the determination is that the applicant is not eligible, the enrolling officer shall notify the applicant in writing, stating the reasons for the refusal and the right to request an exception under Section 8.
6. Responsibilities of Community Health Officers in Verification

Community health officers (CHOs) play a central role in the eligibility verification process under this Policy. The responsibilities set out below are mandatory, and no officer may delegate them to a volunteer, an intern, or any person who has not been accredited by the Program Director for the purpose of verification.

6.1 General Duties

Each CHO assigned to verification duties shall:

- Conduct the home visit required under Step 5 of Section 5 of this Policy, unless the Program Director has approved an alternative method of verification in writing.
- Confirm the identity of each adult household member using a government-issued identification document. Where the applicant or a household member does not possess such a document, the CHO shall record the reason and may accept a sworn affidavit attested to by a local government official or a traditional leader, provided the affidavit is dated within three months of the application.
- Record the household composition on Form HSP-HV-01, noting the name, age, sex, and relation to the applicant of each person residing at the address at the time of the visit.
- Observe and note the general condition of the dwelling, including the type of roofing, wall material, and access to water and sanitation. These observations shall be recorded in the remarks section of Form HSP-HV-01 and shall not, on their own, be used to determine eligibility.
- Verify that the applicant's place of residence falls within the catchment area of the participating health facility named in the Expression of Interest. Where the residence is on a boundary, the CHO shall mark the location on a sketch map and attach it to the form.
- Collect, where the applicant has consented, a mobile telephone number and an alternative contact number for the purpose of follow-up communications. Consent shall be recorded on Form HSP-CN-01.
- Explain to the applicant the purpose of the verification, the documents required, and the consequences of providing false information. The explanation shall be given in a language the applicant understands, and the CHO shall note on the form which language was used.

6.2 Handling of Incomplete Information

Where the applicant or a household member is unable to provide a required document or where information supplied is incomplete, the CHO shall not reject the application on that basis alone. Instead, the CHO shall:

- Issue a written notice to the applicant listing the missing document or information, and allow the applicant ten working days from the date of the notice to provide it.
- Where the applicant is unable to obtain a document from an issuing authority within the ten working day period, the applicant may apply in writing for a single extension of up to a further ten working days. The CHO may grant such an extension where the applicant has demonstrated a genuine effort to obtain the document.
- Where, after the extension period, the document or information has still not been provided, the CHO shall record the outstanding item on Form HSP-EL-01 and refer the file to the Program Director with a recommendation. The Program Director shall decide whether to proceed with the application on the basis of available evidence or to close the file. The applicant shall be notified in writing of the decision and of the right to reapply.
- Where the applicant states that a document has been lost or destroyed, the CHO may accept a copy of the document, provided the applicant provides a sworn affidavit explaining the loss and confirming that the copy is a true reproduction of the original. The CHO shall sight the copy against any available secondary evidence, such as a photograph, a previous application, or a letter from the issuing authority.
7. Appeals

7.1 Right to Appeal

An applicant, or a household member acting on behalf of the applicant, may appeal a decision to deny enrollment, to close a file, or to remove a household member from the program. The right to appeal also applies where the Program Director has decided to proceed with an application on the basis of available evidence under section 6.2 and the applicant considers that the decision was made without full consideration of the available information.

The appeal shall be considered on the basis of the information available at the time of the original decision, together with any new information the applicant submits with the appeal. The appeals process is administrative and does not create a right to legal representation at the expense of the Program.

7.2 Grounds for Appeal

An appeal may be submitted on one or more of the following grounds:

- The decision was based on an error of fact, including incorrect recording of income, household composition, or residency.
- The decision was based on an error in the application of the eligibility criteria set out in Section 3 of this Policy.
- The decision failed to take into account relevant information that was available at the time of the decision.
- New information has become available that could reasonably have affected the original decision.
- The applicant was not given a fair opportunity to provide required information or to respond to a notice issued under Section 6.

7.3 Timeframe for Submitting an Appeal

An appeal must be submitted in writing within fifteen working days of the date of the written decision being appealed. The date of the decision shall be the date printed on the notification letter. Where the applicant can demonstrate that the notification was not received, the fifteen working day period shall run from the date the applicant first became aware of the decision.

The Program Director may accept an appeal submitted after the fifteen working day period where the applicant demonstrates that the delay was due to circumstances beyond the applicant's control, including serious illness, travel disruption, or other compelling reasons. A request for late acceptance shall be made in writing and shall include an explanation of the reasons for the delay. The Program Director shall respond to a request for late acceptance within five working days.

7.4 How to Submit an Appeal

The appeal shall be submitted in writing to the Program Director at the address stated on the decision letter, or by hand to any Healthy Start enrolment centre. The appeal shall include:

- The name and address of the applicant and the applicant's unique application reference number, where known.
- The date of the decision being appealed.
- A clear statement of the grounds for appeal.
- A copy of the decision letter, where available.
- Any supporting documents or information the applicant wishes the appeal committee to consider.

An appeal may be submitted by a representative acting on behalf of the applicant, provided the representative includes written authorisation from the applicant. The authorisation shall be signed by the applicant and shall state the name of the representative and the extent of the representative's authority.

7.5 Acknowledgment of Appeal

The Program Director shall acknowledge receipt of an appeal in writing within five working days of receipt. The acknowledgment shall include:

- The date of receipt of the appeal.
- The name of the officer assigned to review the appeal.
- An estimate of the time within which a decision on the appeal is expected.
8. Monitoring and Evaluation of Eligibility Criteria

8.1 Purpose of Monitoring

The Program Director shall establish a system for the ongoing monitoring of the implementation of this policy. The purpose of monitoring shall be to:

- Ensure that eligibility determinations are made consistently and in accordance with the criteria set out in this policy.
- Identify any unintended barriers to enrolment arising from the application of the criteria.
- Assess whether the criteria continue to reflect the health needs of the communities served by the Healthy Start program.
- Provide information to inform any future revision of this policy.

8.2 Review Schedule

A formal review of this policy shall be undertaken at least once every twelve months. The review shall be conducted by the Program Director in consultation with the State Health Officer, the Community Health Outreach Coordinator, and such other officers as the Program Director considers appropriate.

In addition to the annual review, the Program Director may initiate a review of this policy at any time where:

- The State Ministry of Health issues new guidance or directives concerning maternal and child health programmes.
- An evaluation of program outcomes identifies significant disparities in access or enrolment across districts.
- The appeal committee reports recurring issues in the application of the eligibility criteria.
- Funding arrangements for the program change in a manner that affects enrolment targets or service scope.

8.3 Data Collection for Monitoring

The following data shall be collected and maintained for the purpose of monitoring:

- The number of applications received, disaggregated by ward and by local government area.
- The number of applications approved, deferred, and denied, with reasons for denial recorded in the application file.
- The number of appeals submitted and the outcome of each appeal.
- The average time taken from receipt of application to the communication of the decision.
- The number of beneficiaries who fail to complete enrolment within the prescribed period and the reasons for such failure, where known.

Data shall be recorded in the Healthy Start Management Information System. Field staff shall ensure that all data entries are completed within five working days of the relevant event. Where data is recorded on paper forms prior to entry into the system, the paper forms shall be retained in the relevant office file for a period of not less than three years.

8.4 Use of Monitoring Data

The Program Director shall prepare a monitoring report on a quarterly basis. The report shall include a summary of the data referred to in section 8.3, together with any observations on trends or anomalies. The report shall be submitted to the State Health Officer and shall be made available to the Community Health Outreach Coordinator.

Findings from the monitoring report shall be used to inform training for enrolment officers, to adjust outreach activities, and to identify areas where this policy may require clarification or amendment.

8.5 Evaluation of Program Outcomes

In addition to the monitoring of eligibility determinations, the Program Director shall arrange for an evaluation of program outcomes to be conducted at least once every two years. The evaluation shall examine, among other things:

- The health impact of the program on enrolled beneficiaries.
- The coverage of the program relative to the target population in each local government area.
- The retention of beneficiaries in the program, including the number of beneficiaries who exit the program and the reasons for exit.
- The cost-effectiveness of the program.

written approval, mileage shall be reimbursed at a rate of 210 NGN per kilometre.

7.3 Mileage claims must be supported by a vehicle log sheet showing the odometer
reading at the start and end of the journey, the route taken, and the purpose of the
trip.

7.4 For intercity travel by public transport, reimbursement shall be made upon
submission of valid tickets or receipts. Where tickets are not available, the staff
member may claim the actual fare paid, supported by a written declaration.

8. Expense Claim Procedure

8.1 All claims for per diem, lodging, transportation, and other approved expenses
must be submitted on the standard HBCHI Expense Claim Form (Form FIN-04) within 14
days of the end of the assignment.

8.2 The completed form must be accompanied by all original receipts, the approved
Travel Authorisation (Form FIN-02), and any other supporting documentation.

8.3 Claims submitted more than 14 days after the end of the assignment shall be
subject to a written explanation and may be declined at the discretion of the Finance
Officer.
**8. Expense Claim Procedure (continued)**

8.4 The Finance Officer shall review each claim for completeness and accuracy. Where
arithmetical errors are identified, the claim shall be returned to the staff member for
correction before payment is processed. Handwritten corrections must be initialled by
the staff member making the correction.

8.5 Payment of approved claims shall be made by bank transfer to the staff member's
designated salary account within 21 working days of the date of submission of a
complete and correct claim.

8.6 Claims for amounts less than 5,000 NGN may be paid in cash at the discretion of the
Finance Officer, provided that the staff member signs the cash payment voucher.

8.7 No claim shall be processed without a valid Travel Authorisation (Form FIN-02)
approved prior to the commencement of the assignment. Retroactive authorisation shall
only be considered in exceptional circumstances, with justification documented in
writing by the requesting staff member and approved by the Executive Director.

**9. Per Diem Policy 2024**

The following rates and provisions apply to all field assignments commencing on or
after 1 January 2024. This policy is the current version and supersedes all earlier
revisions. Staff members assigned in the 2023 calendar year but whose assignments
continue into 2024 shall be paid at the 2024 rate for days worked on or after
1 January 2024.

| Item | Rate / Provision |
|------|------------------|
| Per diem rate (standard, all locations) | 18,000 NGN per day |
| Per diem rate (half-day, 4–8 hours in the field) | 9,000 NGN per day |
| Per diem rate (less than 4 hours) | Nil |
| Weekly rest day (Friday) per diem | 18,000 NGN per day (full rate applies) |

Per Diem Policy 2024 per_diem_rate_naira_per_day is 18000 NGN/day. Record status: current.

9.1 The per diem rate is intended to cover meals and incidental expenses while on
field assignment. Staff are not required to submit receipts for the per diem portion
of their claim.

9.2 Per diem is payable for each full day of the assignment, including travel days,
provided that the staff member is away from their duty station overnight. For
assignments where the staff member returns to the duty station on the same day, the
half-day rate shall apply where the time away from the station is between 4 and 8
hours.

9.3 The weekly rest day (Friday) is a working day for field purposes in many of the
LGAs we operate in. Where a staff member is in the field on a Friday, the full per
diem rate of 18,000 NGN shall be paid. This does not apply to public holidays
observed by HBCHI.

9.4 No per diem shall be payable for any day on which the staff member is on leave
or is suspended from duty, even if the assignment dates have been extended to
accommodate such absence.

**10. Mileage and Fuel Advance**

10.1 For staff using personal vehicles with prior written approval, the mileage
reimbursement rate for 2024 is 220 NGN per kilometre. This rate applies to official
duty travel only, as recorded in the vehicle log sheet.

10.2 Fuel advances may be requested for project vehicles prior to a field
assignment. The advance shall be calculated at the rate of 12 litres per 100
kilometres, using the planned route distance. The advance must be reconciled against
actual fuel receipts within 7 days of the end of the assignment.

10.3 Any unused fuel advance shall be refunded to HBCHI by deduction from the next
payable claim. Any shortfall in fuel due to unauthorised use of the project vehicle
shall be recovered from the staff member's salary.
**11. Expense Approval Authorities**

11.1 All expense claims, including per diem, mileage reimbursement, fuel advances, and any
other travel-related costs, must be submitted on the standard HBCHI Expense Claim Form
(ECF-2024). Claims must be accompanied by the relevant travel authorization, vehicle log
extract, and receipts as required by Sections 9 and 10 above.

11.2 The following approval thresholds apply to all claims and expenses incurred for
official HBCHI business. No expense may be incurred or reimbursed without the approval of
the designated authority for the amount in question.

| **Expense Amount (NGN)** | **Approval Required By** |
|--------------------------|--------------------------|
| Up to 50,000 | Line Manager / Zonal Coordinator |
| 50,001 – 200,000 | Program Manager |
| 200,001 – 500,000 | Deputy Program Director |
| Above 500,000 | Dr. Amina Bello (Program Director) |

11.3 Dr. Amina Bello signature_authority_for_expense_approval is Dr. Amina Bello. Record status: current. This
designation is current for the 2024 policy year. No other officer, irrespective of title or
seniority, is authorised to approve expenses above 500,000 NGN.

11.4 For expenses between 200,001 and 500,000 NGN, the Deputy Program Director may
approve, but the claim must be copied to the finance officer for record. For expenses above
500,000 NGN, the claim must be countersigned by the finance officer after Dr. Bello's
approval, before payment is processed.

11.5 No expense shall be split into smaller amounts for the purpose of avoiding the
approval thresholds in the table above. Any attempt to split an expense shall result in the
claim being returned to the submitter and may be treated as a disciplinary matter.

**12. Approval Process**

12.1 The approval process for all travel-related expenses shall be as follows:

a) The staff member submits the completed ECF-2024 with all supporting documents to
their line manager within 10 working days of the end of the assignment.

b) The line manager reviews the claim for completeness, accuracy of arithmetic, and
compliance with the travel authorization. The line manager shall verify that the dates
on the claim match the dates on the travel authorization and the vehicle log.

c) The line manager forwards the claim, with a signed recommendation, to the
appropriate approval authority as per the thresholds in Section 11.2.

d) The approval authority reviews the claim and, if satisfied, signs the approval box
on the ECF-2024. The approval authority is responsible for confirming the claim is
within the approved budget line for the program.

e) The approved claim is forwarded to the finance officer for payment. The finance
officer shall verify the approval signature and the arithmetic before processing
payment.

12.2 All approvals must be documented. The approval signature, date of approval, and the
designation of the approving officer must be legible on the ECF-2024. Where the approval
is given electronically, the email authorisation must be printed and attached to the claim.

12.3 Approval authorities shall not approve their own claims. Where the claimant is the
Program Director, the claim shall be approved by the HBCHI Executive Director or the
Board Treasurer, as applicable.

12.4 Where an approval authority is absent from the station for more than 5 working
days, they shall delegate their approval authority in writing to the next senior officer.
The delegation must be filed with the finance officer before it is exercised. A delegated
authority shall not approve a claim above the threshold of the delegating officer.
**13. Mileage Reimbursement**

13.1 Staff using their personal vehicles for official HBCHI business may claim mileage at the rates set out in the table below. These rates are effective from 1 January 2024 and apply to all journeys undertaken on or after that date. Claims for journeys undertaken prior to 1 January 2024 shall be paid at the rates in force at the time of travel.

| Vehicle Type | Rate per Kilometre (₦) |
|:---|:---|
| Motorcycle (100cc – 200cc) | 45.00 |
| Motorcycle (above 200cc) | 55.00 |
| Saloon car (up to 1.6L engine) | 85.00 |
| Saloon car (above 1.6L engine) | 110.00 |
| SUV / Pickup (4-wheel drive) | 140.00 |
| Van / Minibus (up to 12 seats) | 160.00 |

13.2 The rate per kilometre is inclusive of fuel, oil, routine maintenance, and wear and tear on the vehicle. No separate claim for fuel or lubricants shall be entertained where mileage is claimed for the same journey.

13.3 Mileage shall be calculated using the shortest practicable route between the duty station and the place of assignment, unless the travel authorization expressly permits a longer route due to road conditions, security, or an approved stopover. The distance used must be stated on the claim form, and the line manager may require a route map or odometer reading to confirm the distance.

13.4 Where the vehicle is used for more than one official purpose on the same day, the odometer reading at the start and end of each journey must be recorded in the vehicle log. The total distance claimed shall not exceed the sum of the recorded journeys.

13.5 Staff travelling on official duty in an HBCHI-owned or HBCHI-hired vehicle shall not claim mileage. They may, however, claim the actual cost of fuel where the vehicle was not fuelled from the HBCHI bulk fuel account and receipts are attached.

13.6 The Finance Officer may adjust the mileage rates annually by notice in writing. Any adjustment shall take effect from 1 January of the following year. The rates in Section 13.1 shall remain in force until such notice is issued.

**14. Receipts and Supporting Documentation**

14.1 All expenses claimed must be supported by original receipts. Photocopies, scanned copies, or mobile photographs of receipts shall not be accepted unless the original receipt has been lost and the staff member submits a signed declaration of loss together with the copy.

14.2 A receipt must show the following information to be acceptable:

a) The name and address of the vendor or service provider;

b) The date of the transaction;

c) A description of the goods or services purchased;

d) The amount paid, in Naira;

e) The vendor's signature or stamp, where the vendor customarily provides one.

14.3 Where a receipt is for a transaction that includes both official and personal items, the official portion must be clearly identified and the personal portion must be shown separately. The claim shall be limited to the official portion.

14.4 Receipts for accommodation must be itemised to show the room rate, taxes, and any other charges separately. A receipt that only shows a lump sum shall be returned to the staff member for itemisation.

14.5 Where a staff member is unable to obtain a receipt for a small expense (for example, a roadside toll or a local transport fare of ₦2,000 or less), they may attach a written explanation. The line manager may accept the explanation where the amount is reasonable and the expense is consistent with the nature of the assignment. This concession does not apply to accommodation, fuel, or vehicle hire.
**15. Submission of Expense Claims**

15.1 A staff member shall submit an expense claim within fourteen (14) working days of the completion of the journey or the incurring of the expense, whichever is later. Claims submitted after this period shall be accepted only with the written approval of the Director of Programmes.

15.2 Claims shall be submitted on the standard HBCHI Expense Claim Form (Form EC-1). The form shall be completed in full, with all sections filled in. Incomplete forms shall be returned to the staff member without processing.

15.3 The following documents shall be attached to the claim, as applicable:

a) The approved Travel Authorisation Form (Form TA-2);

b) Original receipts as required under Section 14;

c) A copy of the duty call or assignment letter;

d) The vehicle log sheet, where a vehicle was used;

e) A signed declaration of loss, where any original receipt has been lost;

f) Any other supporting document required by the Finance Officer.

15.4 The staff member shall sign and date the claim form. The signature certifies that the expenses claimed were actually incurred, that the amounts are correct, and that no part of the claim has been or will be claimed from any other source.

15.5 The claim shall be submitted to the staff member's line manager for review and approval. The line manager shall check the claim against the approved travel authorisation, the duty call, and the supporting receipts. The line manager shall note any discrepancies on the claim form and return it to the staff member for correction where necessary.

15.6 After the line manager has approved the claim, it shall be forwarded to the Finance Officer for verification and payment. The Finance Officer may request additional information or documentation where the claim is not clear.

**16. Approval of Claims**

16.1 All claims must be approved before payment is made. No payment shall be made on the basis of an unapproved claim.

16.2 The approval authority for expense claims is as follows:

a) For claims of ₦50,000 or less: the line manager;

b) For claims above ₦50,000 and up to ₦200,000: the Finance Officer, in addition to the line manager;

c) For claims above ₦200,000 and up to ₦500,000: the Executive Director, in addition to the Finance Officer and the line manager;

d) For claims above ₦500,000: the Board of Directors, through a resolution at a meeting or by written circular, in addition to the Executive Director, the Finance Officer, and the line manager.

16.3 Where the staff member submitting the claim is the Executive Director, the claim shall be approved by the Chair of the Board of Directors or, in the Chair's absence, the Deputy Chair.

16.4 Where the staff member submitting the claim is the Finance Officer, the claim shall be approved by the Executive Director. The Finance Officer shall not approve their own claim.

16.5 The approving officer shall sign and date the claim form and shall indicate the amount approved. Where the approving officer reduces an amount, the reason for the reduction shall be stated in writing on the claim form.

16.6 A staff member who is aggrieved by a reduction or a rejection of a claim may appeal in writing to the next higher approving authority within seven (7) working days of receiving the decision. The appeal shall state the grounds for the appeal and shall attach any additional supporting documents.

**17. Payment of Claims**

17.1 Approved claims shall be processed for payment by the Finance Officer. Payment shall be made by bank transfer to the staff member's salary account, unless the Finance Officer directs otherwise in writing.

Where the number of applications exceeds available program slots, priority will be given to applicants who fall within one or more of the following categories. Priority categories are listed in descending order of precedence:

a) Applicants under the age of 18 years (adolescent pregnancies).

b) Applicants over the age of 35 years (advanced maternal age).

c) Applicants with a history of complicated pregnancy, including but not limited to: previous caesarean section, pre-eclampsia, eclampsia, gestational diabetes, or postpartum hemorrhage.

d) Applicants with a known chronic illness, such as hypertension, diabetes, HIV, or sickle cell disease.

e) Applicants from households with a monthly income below the national minimum wage, or households that are food-insecure as determined by the HBCHI household screening tool.

f) Applicants with no prior antenatal care in any facility during the current pregnancy.

3.3 Ineligibility

An applicant shall be deemed ineligible if any of the following conditions apply:

a) The applicant is not a resident of the operational catchment area as defined in Section 3.1(b).

b) The applicant is not pregnant and does not have an infant under six (6) months of age.

c) The applicant has previously been disenrolled from the Healthy Start Program for cause, including but not limited to fraud, misrepresentation of information, or repeated non-compliance with program requirements. Disenrollment for cause shall be permanent unless the applicant successfully appeals the decision through the process outlined in Section 7.

d) The applicant has been found to have provided false or misleading information on the application form or during the verification process. Such applicants shall be barred from re-applying for a period of twelve (12) months from the date of discovery.

5.3 Certified Clinic Definition

For the purposes of this policy, a certified clinic is a health facility that meets the following criteria:

a) It is registered with the State Ministry of Health or the relevant local government health authority.

b) It has at least one qualified midwife, nurse, or community health officer on staff who is trained in antenatal care.

c) It has the basic equipment and supplies needed to conduct antenatal examinations, including a blood pressure machine, a fetoscope or Doppler, and weighing scales.

d) It has been certified by the HBCHI program office as a participating clinic for the Healthy Start Program. A list of certified clinics is maintained by the program office and is available to all enrolling officers. The list is updated quarterly.

A clinic that is registered with the State Ministry of Health but has not been certified by the HBCHI program office is not considered a certified clinic for the purposes of this policy. However, an applicant who has attended an antenatal visit at such a clinic may still be eligible if the clinic is subsequently certified before the date of the applicant's enrollment. In such cases, the enrolling officer shall note the certification date in the applicant's file.

5.4 Verification of Clinic Certification

Healthy Start Program eligibility_requires_antenatal_visit is at least one antenatal visit at a certified clinic. Record status: current.

Enrolling officers shall verify the certification status of a clinic using the following methods:

a) Consult the current list of certified clinics, which is available in the program office and on the HBCHI intranet. The list is updated quarterly, and the date of the last update shall be noted on the list.

b) If the clinic is not on the list, the enrolling officer shall contact the program office by phone or email to confirm whether the clinic has been certified. The program office shall respond within two working days.

c) If the clinic is not certified, the applicant shall be informed that the antenatal visit does not meet the requirement. The applicant shall be given the opportunity to attend an antenatal visit at a certified clinic before the application deadline, if time permits.

d) In cases where the applicant has attended an antenatal visit at a clinic that is not certified, but the applicant is otherwise eligible, the enrolling officer may recommend that the applicant be allowed to enroll on a provisional basis, subject to the applicant attending a first antenatal visit at a certified clinic within four weeks of enrollment. Provisional enrollment is at the discretion of the program director and shall be documented in the applicant's file.

5.5 Timing of the Antenatal Visit

The antenatal visit must have occurred within the current pregnancy. For applicants who are not yet pregnant but are applying for the program as part of family planning or preconception care, the antenatal visit requirement is waived. In such cases, the applicant shall be referred for a first antenatal visit upon becoming pregnant.

For applicants who are pregnant but have not yet attended any antenatal visit, the requirement is not waived. The applicant must attend at least one antenatal visit at a certified clinic before the application can be approved. The enrolling officer shall refer the applicant to a certified clinic and shall note the referral in the applicant's file. The applicant shall provide proof of the visit within two weeks of the referral, or before the application deadline, whichever is earlier.

9. ENROLLMENT PROCEDURE

The enrollment procedure is set out below. The steps are to be followed in the order given, and no step may be omitted or reordered without the prior written approval of the Program Director.

Step 1 – Expression of Interest. An applicant who wishes to enrol in the Healthy Start Program shall submit a written Expression of Interest to the enrolling officer at the health facility nearest to the applicant's place of residence. The Expression of Interest may be submitted in person or by post. It shall include the applicant's full name, date of birth, address, and the name of the head of household, if the applicant is a minor or is applying as part of a household.

Step 2 – Preliminary Screening. Upon receipt of the Expression of Interest, the enrolling officer shall conduct a preliminary screening to determine whether the applicant appears to meet the eligibility criteria set out in Sections 3, 4, and 5 of this Policy. The preliminary screening shall be based solely on the information contained in the Expression of Interest and any supporting documents submitted with it. The enrolling officer shall not require the applicant to provide additional information at this stage unless the Expression of Interest is incomplete on its face.

Step 3 – Invitation to Apply. Where the preliminary screening indicates that the applicant may be eligible, the enrolling officer shall issue a formal Application Form (Form HSP-AP-01) to the applicant. The Application Form shall be issued within five working days of the preliminary screening. Where the preliminary screening indicates that the applicant is not eligible, the enrolling officer shall notify the applicant in writing of the reasons for the refusal, and shall inform the applicant of the right to request an exception under Section 8 of this Policy.

Step 4 – Submission of Application. The applicant shall complete the Application Form and return it to the enrolling officer, together with the supporting documents listed in Section 7 of this Policy. The application shall be submitted within twenty working days of the date of issue of the Application Form. If the application is not submitted within this period, the invitation to apply shall lapse, and the applicant shall be required to begin the process again with a new Expression of Interest.

Step 5 – Verification. On receipt of the completed Application Form, the enrolling officer shall verify the information contained in it. The verification shall include, where practicable, a home visit to confirm the applicant's place of residence and household composition. The enrolling officer shall also verify the authenticity of the supporting documents, and may contact the issuing authorities for this purpose. The verification shall be completed within fifteen working days of receipt of the application.

Step 6 – Eligibility Determination. Upon completion of the verification, the enrolling officer shall determine whether the applicant meets the eligibility criteria. The determination shall be recorded on Form HSP-EL-01, which shall be signed and dated by the enrolling officer. Where the determination is that the applicant is eligible, the enrolling officer shall forward the file to the Program Director's office for final approval. Where the determination is that the applicant is not eligible, the enrolling officer shall notify the applicant in writing, stating the reasons for the refusal and the right to request an exception under Section 8.

6. Responsibilities of Community Health Officers in Verification

Community health officers (CHOs) play a central role in the eligibility verification process under this Policy. The responsibilities set out below are mandatory, and no officer may delegate them to a volunteer, an intern, or any person who has not been accredited by the Program Director for the purpose of verification.

6.1 General Duties

Each CHO assigned to verification duties shall:

- Conduct the home visit required under Step 5 of Section 5 of this Policy, unless the Program Director has approved an alternative method of verification in writing.
- Confirm the identity of each adult household member using a government-issued identification document. Where the applicant or a household member does not possess such a document, the CHO shall record the reason and may accept a sworn affidavit attested to by a local government official or a traditional leader, provided the affidavit is dated within three months of the application.
- Record the household composition on Form HSP-HV-01, noting the name, age, sex, and relation to the applicant of each person residing at the address at the time of the visit.
- Observe and note the general condition of the dwelling, including the type of roofing, wall material, and access to water and sanitation. These observations shall be recorded in the remarks section of Form HSP-HV-01 and shall not, on their own, be used to determine eligibility.
- Verify that the applicant's place of residence falls within the catchment area of the participating health facility named in the Expression of Interest. Where the residence is on a boundary, the CHO shall mark the location on a sketch map and attach it to the form.
- Collect, where the applicant has consented, a mobile telephone number and an alternative contact number for the purpose of follow-up communications. Consent shall be recorded on Form HSP-CN-01.
- Explain to the applicant the purpose of the verification, the documents required, and the consequences of providing false information. The explanation shall be given in a language the applicant understands, and the CHO shall note on the form which language was used.

6.2 Handling of Incomplete Information

Where the applicant or a household member is unable to provide a required document or where information supplied is incomplete, the CHO shall not reject the application on that basis alone. Instead, the CHO shall:

- Issue a written notice to the applicant listing the missing document or information, and allow the applicant ten working days from the date of the notice to provide it.
- Where the applicant is unable to obtain a document from an issuing authority within the ten working day period, the applicant may apply in writing for a single extension of up to a further ten working days. The CHO may grant such an extension where the applicant has demonstrated a genuine effort to obtain the document.
- Where, after the extension period, the document or information has still not been provided, the CHO shall record the outstanding item on Form HSP-EL-01 and refer the file to the Program Director with a recommendation. The Program Director shall decide whether to proceed with the application on the basis of available evidence or to close the file. The applicant shall be notified in writing of the decision and of the right to reapply.
- Where the applicant states that a document has been lost or destroyed, the CHO may accept a copy of the document, provided the applicant provides a sworn affidavit explaining the loss and confirming that the copy is a true reproduction of the original. The CHO shall sight the copy against any available secondary evidence, such as a photograph, a previous application, or a letter from the issuing authority.

7. Appeals

7.1 Right to Appeal

An applicant, or a household member acting on behalf of the applicant, may appeal a decision to deny enrollment, to close a file, or to remove a household member from the program. The right to appeal also applies where the Program Director has decided to proceed with an application on the basis of available evidence under section 6.2 and the applicant considers that the decision was made without full consideration of the available information.

The appeal shall be considered on the basis of the information available at the time of the original decision, together with any new information the applicant submits with the appeal. The appeals process is administrative and does not create a right to legal representation at the expense of the Program.

7.2 Grounds for Appeal

An appeal may be submitted on one or more of the following grounds:

- The decision was based on an error of fact, including incorrect recording of income, household composition, or residency.
- The decision was based on an error in the application of the eligibility criteria set out in Section 3 of this Policy.
- The decision failed to take into account relevant information that was available at the time of the decision.
- New information has become available that could reasonably have affected the original decision.
- The applicant was not given a fair opportunity to provide required information or to respond to a notice issued under Section 6.

7.3 Timeframe for Submitting an Appeal

An appeal must be submitted in writing within fifteen working days of the date of the written decision being appealed. The date of the decision shall be the date printed on the notification letter. Where the applicant can demonstrate that the notification was not received, the fifteen working day period shall run from the date the applicant first became aware of the decision.

The Program Director may accept an appeal submitted after the fifteen working day period where the applicant demonstrates that the delay was due to circumstances beyond the applicant's control, including serious illness, travel disruption, or other compelling reasons. A request for late acceptance shall be made in writing and shall include an explanation of the reasons for the delay. The Program Director shall respond to a request for late acceptance within five working days.

7.4 How to Submit an Appeal

The appeal shall be submitted in writing to the Program Director at the address stated on the decision letter, or by hand to any Healthy Start enrolment centre. The appeal shall include:

- The name and address of the applicant and the applicant's unique application reference number, where known.
- The date of the decision being appealed.
- A clear statement of the grounds for appeal.
- A copy of the decision letter, where available.
- Any supporting documents or information the applicant wishes the appeal committee to consider.

An appeal may be submitted by a representative acting on behalf of the applicant, provided the representative includes written authorisation from the applicant. The authorisation shall be signed by the applicant and shall state the name of the representative and the extent of the representative's authority.

7.5 Acknowledgment of Appeal

The Program Director shall acknowledge receipt of an appeal in writing within five working days of receipt. The acknowledgment shall include:

- The date of receipt of the appeal.
- The name of the officer assigned to review the appeal.
- An estimate of the time within which a decision on the appeal is expected.

8. Monitoring and Evaluation of Eligibility Criteria

8.1 Purpose of Monitoring

The Program Director shall establish a system for the ongoing monitoring of the implementation of this policy. The purpose of monitoring shall be to:

- Ensure that eligibility determinations are made consistently and in accordance with the criteria set out in this policy.
- Identify any unintended barriers to enrolment arising from the application of the criteria.
- Assess whether the criteria continue to reflect the health needs of the communities served by the Healthy Start program.
- Provide information to inform any future revision of this policy.

8.2 Review Schedule

A formal review of this policy shall be undertaken at least once every twelve months. The review shall be conducted by the Program Director in consultation with the State Health Officer, the Community Health Outreach Coordinator, and such other officers as the Program Director considers appropriate.

In addition to the annual review, the Program Director may initiate a review of this policy at any time where:

- The State Ministry of Health issues new guidance or directives concerning maternal and child health programmes.
- An evaluation of program outcomes identifies significant disparities in access or enrolment across districts.
- The appeal committee reports recurring issues in the application of the eligibility criteria.
- Funding arrangements for the program change in a manner that affects enrolment targets or service scope.

8.3 Data Collection for Monitoring

The following data shall be collected and maintained for the purpose of monitoring:

- The number of applications received, disaggregated by ward and by local government area.
- The number of applications approved, deferred, and denied, with reasons for denial recorded in the application file.
- The number of appeals submitted and the outcome of each appeal.
- The average time taken from receipt of application to the communication of the decision.
- The number of beneficiaries who fail to complete enrolment within the prescribed period and the reasons for such failure, where known.

Data shall be recorded in the Healthy Start Management Information System. Field staff shall ensure that all data entries are completed within five working days of the relevant event. Where data is recorded on paper forms prior to entry into the system, the paper forms shall be retained in the relevant office file for a period of not less than three years.

8.4 Use of Monitoring Data

The Program Director shall prepare a monitoring report on a quarterly basis. The report shall include a summary of the data referred to in section 8.3, together with any observations on trends or anomalies. The report shall be submitted to the State Health Officer and shall be made available to the Community Health Outreach Coordinator.

Findings from the monitoring report shall be used to inform training for enrolment officers, to adjust outreach activities, and to identify areas where this policy may require clarification or amendment.

8.5 Evaluation of Program Outcomes

In addition to the monitoring of eligibility determinations, the Program Director shall arrange for an evaluation of program outcomes to be conducted at least once every two years. The evaluation shall examine, among other things:

- The health impact of the program on enrolled beneficiaries.
- The coverage of the program relative to the target population in each local government area.
- The retention of beneficiaries in the program, including the number of beneficiaries who exit the program and the reasons for exit.
- The cost-effectiveness of the program.

staff member is away for more than 12 hours.

5.2 For assignments lasting less than 12 hours but more than 6 hours, the staff member
shall receive 50% of the daily per diem rate.

an official assignment.

hotel or guesthouse.

**11. Expense Approval Authorities**

11.1 All expense claims, including per diem, mileage reimbursement, fuel advances, and any
other travel-related costs, must be submitted on the standard HBCHI Expense Claim Form
(ECF-2024). Claims must be accompanied by the relevant travel authorization, vehicle log
extract, and receipts as required by Sections 9 and 10 above.

11.2 The following approval thresholds apply to all claims and expenses incurred for
official HBCHI business. No expense may be incurred or reimbursed without the approval of
the designated authority for the amount in question.

| **Expense Amount (NGN)** | **Approval Required By** |
|--------------------------|--------------------------|
| Up to 50,000 | Line Manager / Zonal Coordinator |
| 50,001 – 200,000 | Program Manager |
| 200,001 – 500,000 | Deputy Program Director |
| Above 500,000 | Dr. Amina Bello (Program Director) |

11.3 Dr. Amina Bello signature_authority_for_expense_approval is Dr. Amina Bello. Record status: current. This
designation is current for the 2024 policy year. No other officer, irrespective of title or
seniority, is authorised to approve expenses above 500,000 NGN.

11.4 For expenses between 200,001 and 500,000 NGN, the Deputy Program Director may
approve, but the claim must be copied to the finance officer for record. For expenses above
500,000 NGN, the claim must be countersigned by the finance officer after Dr. Bello's
approval, before payment is processed.

11.5 No expense shall be split into smaller amounts for the purpose of avoiding the
approval thresholds in the table above. Any attempt to split an expense shall result in the
claim being returned to the submitter and may be treated as a disciplinary matter.

**12. Approval Process**

12.1 The approval process for all travel-related expenses shall be as follows:

a) The staff member submits the completed ECF-2024 with all supporting documents to
their line manager within 10 working days of the end of the assignment.

b) The line manager reviews the claim for completeness, accuracy of arithmetic, and
compliance with the travel authorization. The line manager shall verify that the dates
on the claim match the dates on the travel authorization and the vehicle log.

c) The line manager forwards the claim, with a signed recommendation, to the
appropriate approval authority as per the thresholds in Section 11.2.

d) The approval authority reviews the claim and, if satisfied, signs the approval box
on the ECF-2024. The approval authority is responsible for confirming the claim is
within the approved budget line for the program.

e) The approved claim is forwarded to the finance officer for payment. The finance
officer shall verify the approval signature and the arithmetic before processing
payment.

12.2 All approvals must be documented. The approval signature, date of approval, and the
designation of the approving officer must be legible on the ECF-2024. Where the approval
is given electronically, the email authorisation must be printed and attached to the claim.

12.3 Approval authorities shall not approve their own claims. Where the claimant is the
Program Director, the claim shall be approved by the HBCHI Executive Director or the
Board Treasurer, as applicable.

12.4 Where an approval authority is absent from the station for more than 5 working
days, they shall delegate their approval authority in writing to the next senior officer.
The delegation must be filed with the finance officer before it is exercised. A delegated
authority shall not approve a claim above the threshold of the delegating officer.

**13. Mileage Reimbursement**

13.1 Staff using their personal vehicles for official HBCHI business may claim mileage at the rates set out in the table below. These rates are effective from 1 January 2024 and apply to all journeys undertaken on or after that date. Claims for journeys undertaken prior to 1 January 2024 shall be paid at the rates in force at the time of travel.

| Vehicle Type | Rate per Kilometre (₦) |
|:---|:---|
| Motorcycle (100cc – 200cc) | 45.00 |
| Motorcycle (above 200cc) | 55.00 |
| Saloon car (up to 1.6L engine) | 85.00 |
| Saloon car (above 1.6L engine) | 110.00 |
| SUV / Pickup (4-wheel drive) | 140.00 |
| Van / Minibus (up to 12 seats) | 160.00 |

13.2 The rate per kilometre is inclusive of fuel, oil, routine maintenance, and wear and tear on the vehicle. No separate claim for fuel or lubricants shall be entertained where mileage is claimed for the same journey.

13.3 Mileage shall be calculated using the shortest practicable route between the duty station and the place of assignment, unless the travel authorization expressly permits a longer route due to road conditions, security, or an approved stopover. The distance used must be stated on the claim form, and the line manager may require a route map or odometer reading to confirm the distance.

13.4 Where the vehicle is used for more than one official purpose on the same day, the odometer reading at the start and end of each journey must be recorded in the vehicle log. The total distance claimed shall not exceed the sum of the recorded journeys.

13.5 Staff travelling on official duty in an HBCHI-owned or HBCHI-hired vehicle shall not claim mileage. They may, however, claim the actual cost of fuel where the vehicle was not fuelled from the HBCHI bulk fuel account and receipts are attached.

13.6 The Finance Officer may adjust the mileage rates annually by notice in writing. Any adjustment shall take effect from 1 January of the following year. The rates in Section 13.1 shall remain in force until such notice is issued.

**14. Receipts and Supporting Documentation**

14.1 All expenses claimed must be supported by original receipts. Photocopies, scanned copies, or mobile photographs of receipts shall not be accepted unless the original receipt has been lost and the staff member submits a signed declaration of loss together with the copy.

14.2 A receipt must show the following information to be acceptable:

a) The name and address of the vendor or service provider;

b) The date of the transaction;

c) A description of the goods or services purchased;

d) The amount paid, in Naira;

e) The vendor's signature or stamp, where the vendor customarily provides one.

14.3 Where a receipt is for a transaction that includes both official and personal items, the official portion must be clearly identified and the personal portion must be shown separately. The claim shall be limited to the official portion.

14.4 Receipts for accommodation must be itemised to show the room rate, taxes, and any other charges separately. A receipt that only shows a lump sum shall be returned to the staff member for itemisation.

14.5 Where a staff member is unable to obtain a receipt for a small expense (for example, a roadside toll or a local transport fare of ₦2,000 or less), they may attach a written explanation. The line manager may accept the explanation where the amount is reasonable and the expense is consistent with the nature of the assignment. This concession does not apply to accommodation, fuel, or vehicle hire.
